newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end 5-day losing streak, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end 5-day losing streak, volume thin.

text.p: Tokyo stocks snapped out of their five-day losing streak on Monday, ending on a positive tone. Brokers said, however, that turnover was extremely thin as most investors were on the sidelines, searching for sound reasons to trade on.
The 225-issue Nikkei average was 145.44 points or 0.70 percent higher at 20,885.41. Its December futures added 200 points to settle at 20,970.
"Trade was extremely dull today and the benchmark Nikkei's rise was feeble and not really strong enough to be considered a rebound," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said.
"Public funds are fiercely defending the benchmark, preventing it from falling beneath the 20,000 level, so the downside should be limited," said Haruo Nakaharu, strategist at Toyo Securities.

Although trade was subdued, investors sought shares which posted firm half-year earnings recently such as Toshiba Corp and NEC Corp. The former closed two yen up at 735 yen, and was the most heavily traded issue with 3.289 million shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Second-ranking NEC gained 20 yen to 1,240 yen with a 2.867 million turnover.
Kawasaki Heavy, ranking 14th, edged five yen higher to close at 520 yen.

Advancing issues overtook decliners 718 issues to 318, while 195 issues were unchanged. Sector-wise, railway/bus, mining, transport equipment, sea transport and iron/steel were the main gainers. Retreaters were headed by air transport, real estate, pharmaceuticals and textiles.

In other indices, TOPIX was 7.18 points or 0.46 percent higher at 1,564.94. The Nikkei 300 floated 1.13 points or 0.39 percent higher to 293.12. The second section index lost 2.63 points, or 0.13 percent, to 2,030.01.
Turnover was 11.79 million shares against 11.59 million on Friday.
The over-the-counter index was down 3.69 points or 0.25 percent at 1,502.38 in late Tokyo.
